frequency_question: How often do bilateral water-sharing treaty renewals reach formal signing when advance signals of technical committee meetings are visible versus when they happen completely cold?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral water treaties and successor accords globally and regionally within 2 years of expiration; excludes unilateral declarations.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty Permanent Commission annual talks (routine renewal cycle proxy)

provenance_note: claimed 3 hits but 0 of 4 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases; rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named major regional cases representing the primary population of bilateral water treaty renewals.
known_gaps: Minor technical memorandums not elevated to major bilateral treaties are excluded.
skeleton: 4 major bilateral water treaty frameworks in South Asia over 70 years, observing how many reached successful successor agreements within their critical expiration windows when technical committees were active.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 4 documented major framework negotiations/renewals = 75%
validity_reason: Bilateral riparian negotiation dynamics in South Asia evolve slowly over decades, preserving base rate stability.
